docs.heaping.component: HEAPING is the answer to "may these two become one thing", carried by the piece instead of
worked out about it. Two pieces heap when they name the same pile and never otherwise; what a
name MEANS is the game's business, and the kit never looks inside one.
Left to a desk, that answer becomes a chain of tests about what each piece happens to be — has
it faces, has it a back, what is its value — which is a list somebody has to remember to extend
on the day a fourth kind of piece arrives. Said on the piece, it extends itself.
A chip's denomination belongs IN the name: `chip:25` and `chip:100` are two piles the way a card
and a die are. A card's face does not, and that is deliberate — which faces may lie together is
a rule about the MOMENT a piece arrived, not about the piece, and a rule about a moment cannot
live on a node. `Mechanics/Stack merging` is where that half is answered.
docs.heaping.heap: TWO PAIRS ON A BARE DESK. On the left, two chips of one denomination: they say the same name, so
they are one heap and a handle grows under them. On the right, two chips of different ones: they
do not, so there is no handle and each is only itself.
Then give the right-hand chip the left pile's name from the panel. Nothing about the chip
changed — same picture, same size, same place, still overlapping its neighbour by the same third
— and a handle appears. What decided it was what it calls itself.
